title: Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Fire Hospital
title_original: 국립소방병원의 설립 및 운영에 관한 법률
full_text:
ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF THE NATIONAL FIRE HOSPITAL

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to contribute to the health management of firefighting officials through the medical treatment of firefighting officials, analysis of factors harmful to health arising from their special working environments, and research on diseases, and to contribute to the provision of public health and medical services to the people by establishing and operating the National Fire Hospital. <Amended on 2026.2.27>

Article 2 (Legal personality)
The National Fire Hospital (hereinafter referred to as the "Fire Hospital") shall be a legal entity.

Article 3 (Establishment)
① The Fire Hospital shall be established upon registration of its establishment at the location of its principal office.
② The matters to be registered for establishment under paragraph ① shall be as follows:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Principal office and affiliated institutions;
4. Names and addresses of officers;
5. Method of public notice.

Article 4 (Articles of incorporation)
① The articles of incorporation of the Fire Hospital shall include the following matters:
1. Purpose;
2. Name;
3. Locations of the principal office and affiliated institutions;
4. Matters concerning its business;
5. Matters concerning assets and accounting;
6. Matters concerning the board of directors;
7. Matters concerning its organization, officers, and employees;
8. Matters concerning amendments to the articles of incorporation;
9. Matters concerning dissolution;
10. Method of public notice;
11. Matters concerning the conclusion of agreements for personnel and technical support.
② Any amendment to the articles of incorporation of the Fire Hospital shall require authorization from the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.

Article 5 (Business)
① The Fire Hospital shall conduct the following business:
1. Providing medical treatment to firefighting officials; public officials working at agencies performing firefighting duties under Article 3 of the Framework Act on Firefighting Services; persons undergoing education at firefighting training institutions; and auxiliary firefighting personnel, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "firefighting officials, etc." in this Article);
2. Analyzing factors harmful to health in the special working environments of firefighting officials, etc. and conducting surveys and research on diseases;
3. Conducting special health examinations of firefighting officials under Article 16 of the Framework Act on Health, Safety and Welfare of Firefighting Officials;
4. Providing emergency medical services under Article 2 (2) of the Emergency Medical Service Act;
5. Providing public health and medical services under Article 2 (2) of the Public Health and Medical Services Act;
6. Cooperating with and supporting specialized firefighting treatment centers under Article 10 (2) of the Framework Act on Health, Safety and Welfare of Firefighting Officials;
7. Operating education and training programs for rescue and emergency medical personnel under Article 25 (1) of the Act on 119 Rescue and Emergency Medical Services;
8. Providing health education to firefighting officials, etc. and local residents;
9. Conducting business incidental to the business referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 8;
10. Performing and managing other health and medical services deemed necessary by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.
② Specific persons eligible for medical treatment by the Fire Hospital, the scope of such treatment, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Officers)
① The Fire Hospital shall have not more than nine directors, including one president, and one auditor as its officers. All officers other than the president shall serve on a non-standing basis.
② The president and the auditor shall be appointed by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency as prescribed by the articles of incorporation. <Amended on 2025.4.1>
③ Directors shall consist of persons falling under the following subparagraphs (hereinafter referred to as "ex officio directors") and persons appointed by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency as prescribed by the articles of incorporation. At least two directors other than ex officio directors shall be external persons with extensive knowledge and experience in public health and medical services or expertise in hospital management. <Amended on 2025.4.1, 2025.10.1>
1. The Deputy Commissioner of the National Fire Agency;
2. One person each designated by the head of the relevant agency from among Grade III public officials or general-service public officials in the Senior Civil Service Corps belonging to the Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Ministry of Planning and Budget;
3. The Administrative Vice Governor of Chungcheongbuk-do.
④ The term of office of the president and directors other than ex officio directors shall be three years, and they may be reappointed only once. <Amended on 2025.4.1>
⑤ The term of office of the auditor shall be two years, and the auditor may be reappointed only once.
⑥ The auditor shall prepare a comprehensive audit report each year and submit it to the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency and the board of directors.
⑦ If a vacancy arises during the term of office of the president, a director other than an ex officio director, or the auditor, the term of office of the newly appointed president, director other than an ex officio director, or auditor shall begin anew. <Amended on 2025.4.1>

Article 7 (Disqualifications for officers)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall not serve as an officer of the Fire Hospital:
1. A person who is not a national of the Republic of Korea;
2. A person falling under any of the subparagraphs of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act.

Article 8 (Concurrent positions)
① Where necessary to perform the business under Article 5, an educational public official working at a university under Article 2 (1) of the Higher Education Act, or another person working at a university, research institution, or medical institution, may concurrently perform research or medical treatment duties at the Fire Hospital with permission from the head of the university, research institution, or medical institution to which the person belongs.
② The duties, remuneration, and other matters necessary for holding concurrent positions by persons performing duties at the Fire Hospital under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 9 (President)
① The president shall represent the Fire Hospital, have general control over its affairs, and direct and supervise its employees.
② The president shall not be dismissed against his or her will during the term of office except in any of the following cases:
1. Where the president violates this Act, an order issued under this Act, or the articles of incorporation;
2. Where the president causes disruption to the operation of the Fire Hospital through accounting irregularities, intention, or gross negligence;
3. Where the performance of the president's duties becomes extremely difficult or impossible due to a physical or mental disability;
4. Where the president's performance is poor according to the results of the operational evaluation under Article 20 (1).
③ To dismiss the president on any of the grounds specified in paragraph ②, the board of directors shall adopt a resolution with the approval of at least two thirds of the prescribed number of directors and submit a recommendation for dismissal to the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.
④ Where the president is unable to perform his or her duties due to unavoidable circumstances, a director designated by the articles of incorporation shall act on the president's behalf.

Article 10 (Appointment and dismissal of employees)
① The Fire Hospital shall have the employees necessary for its operation.
② Employees shall be appointed and dismissed by the president as prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 11 (Board of directors)
① The Fire Hospital shall have a board of directors to deliberate on and resolve the following matters:
1. Matters concerning amendments to the articles of incorporation;
2. Matters concerning organization;
3. Matters concerning business plans, budgets, and settlement of accounts;
4. Matters concerning acquisition and disposal of property;
5. Matters concerning management, operation, and use of donations;
6. Other matters prescribed as falling within the authority of the board of directors under this Act or the articles of incorporation in connection with the operation of the Fire Hospital.
② The board of directors shall consist of the president and directors.
③ The president shall convene meetings of the board of directors and serve as its chairperson.
④ Meetings of the board of directors shall open with the attendance of a majority of the incumbent members, and resolutions shall be adopted by the affirmative vote of a majority of the members present.
⑤ The auditor may attend and speak at meetings of the board of directors.
⑥ Matters necessary for the operation of the board of directors shall be prescribed by the articles of incorporation.

Article 12 (Financial resources)
The Fire Hospital shall be operated with revenue from the business under Article 5, contributions under Article 13, donations, and other income.

Article 13 (Contributions or subsidies)
① The State may make contributions or provide subsidies within the budget to cover expenses incurred in the business and operation of the Fire Hospital.
② The Fire Hospital shall submit to the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, by April 30 of each business year, a request for a contribution budget for the following business year, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ An individual, corporation, or organization may contribute money or other property to the Fire Hospital to support its business.

Article 14 (Free loan, etc. of State property)
① Where necessary for the establishment and operation of the Fire Hospital, the State may lend State property free of charge or permit its use free of charge, notwithstanding the State Property Act. <Amended on 2026.2.27>
② Matters concerning the free loan of State property and permission for its use under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on 2026.2.27>

Article 15 (Business year)
The business year of the Fire Hospital shall coincide with the fiscal year of the Government.

Article 16 (Submission, etc. of business plans)
① The Fire Hospital shall prepare and submit a business plan and budget before the commencement of each business year and obtain approval from the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② Where the Fire Hospital intends to change any important part of its business plan or budget under paragraph ①, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, it shall submit in advance a business plan and budget specifying the proposed changes and the reasons therefor and obtain approval from the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.

Article 17 (Submission of statement of accounts)
The Fire Hospital shall prepare a statement of the settlement of revenue and expenditure for each business year, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, have it audited by an accounting corporation under Article 23 of the Certified Public Accountant Act, obtain deliberation and a resolution by the board of directors, and submit it to the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency within two months after the commencement of the following fiscal year.

Article 18 (Business cooperation and conclusion of agreements)
① The Fire Hospital may cooperate with other medical institutions, universities, or research institutions in conducting research, implementing projects, providing technical support, and performing other activities relating to the health management of firefighting officials, etc.
② Where necessary for the business under Article 5, the president may conclude agreements with other medical institutions, universities, or research institutions concerning personnel and technical support.

Article 19 (Entrustment of management and operation)
① The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency may entrust all or part of the management and operation of the Fire Hospital to any of the following entities:
1. A medical corporation established under the Medical Service Act;
2. A corporation established under another Act for education and research in medicine, pharmacy, etc., and for medical treatment.
② Entrustment of the management and operation of the Fire Hospital shall be subject to a resolution by the board of directors.
③ Where the management and operation of the Fire Hospital are entrusted under paragraphs ① and ②, the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall conclude an entrustment contract concerning necessary matters, and the term of entrustment shall be determined by mutual agreement between the entrusting party and the entrusted party.
④ Specific matters necessary for entrustment of management and operation, including the methods, procedures, and terms of entrustment, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Operational evaluation, guidance, and supervision)
① The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall conduct an operational evaluation of the Fire Hospital and take necessary measures according to the results.
② The criteria for operational evaluation under paragraph ① shall include the management status of the Fire Hospital, the performance of the business under Article 5 (1), and customer service.
③ Detailed criteria and procedures for operational evaluation under paragraphs ① and ② and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
④ The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall guide and supervise the affairs of the Fire Hospital and may require it to report matters concerning its affairs, accounting, property, etc., or to submit necessary documents.

Article 21 (Dispatch of public officials)
Where necessary to perform its affairs, the Fire Hospital may request the head of a relevant administrative agency, through the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, to dispatch public officials under the agency's jurisdiction.

Article 22 (Application mutatis mutandis of the Civil Act)
Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions of the Civil Act concerning incorporated foundations shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Fire Hospital.

Article 23 (Duty to maintain confidentiality)
Current or former officers and employees of the Fire Hospital shall not disclose or misappropriate secrets acquired in the course of performing their duties.

Article 24 (Prohibition on use of similar names)
No person other than the Fire Hospital established under this Act shall use the name "National Fire Hospital" or any similar name.

Article 25 (Deemed status as public officials for application of penal provisions)
Officers and employees of the Fire Hospital and officers and employees of corporations engaged in entrusted duties under Article 19 shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.

Article 26 (Penalty provisions)
A person who discloses or misappropriates secrets acquired in the course of performing his or her duties in violation of Article 23 shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

Article 27 (Administrative fines)
① A person who uses the name "National Fire Hospital" or any similar name in violation of Article 24 shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won.
② The administrative fine under paragraph ① shall be imposed and collected by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDA <Act No. 17890, 2021.1.12>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force six months after the date of its promulgation: Provided, That Articles 2 and 6 of these Addenda shall enter into force on the date of promulgation.

Article 2 (Preparation for establishment)
① The Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall establish the National Fire Hospital Establishment Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Establishment Committee") within three months from the date of promulgation of this Act to handle affairs concerning the establishment of the Fire Hospital.
② The Establishment Committee shall consist of not more than seven establishment committee members commissioned by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, and the Deputy Commissioner of the National Fire Agency shall serve as its chairperson.
③ The Establishment Committee shall prepare the articles of incorporation of the Fire Hospital and obtain authorization from the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.
④ Upon obtaining authorization under paragraph ③, the Establishment Committee shall register the establishment of the Fire Hospital without delay under the joint names of its members.
⑤ Upon the appointment of the president of the Fire Hospital, the Establishment Committee shall hand over its affairs to the president without delay.
⑥ Upon completion of the handover under paragraph ⑤, the Establishment Committee shall be deemed dissolved and its members shall be deemed discharged from their commissions.

[Enforcement date: 2021.1.12] Article 2

Article 3 (Succession to rights and obligations)
Upon the enforcement of this Act, the Fire Hospital established under this Act shall comprehensively succeed to the rights and obligations relating to the Fire Hospital that belong to the National Fire Agency.

Article 4 (Budget at the time of establishment)
① Until the budget of the Fire Hospital is finalized at the time of its establishment, the Fire Hospital established under this Act may execute the previous budget under the jurisdiction of the National Fire Agency in accordance with the previous practices.
② Expenses executed under paragraph ① shall be deemed to have been executed pursuant to the budget of the Fire Hospital when that budget is established.

Article 5 (Appointment of president, directors, and auditor at the time of establishment)
Notwithstanding Article 6 (2), the president, directors, and auditor at the time of establishment of the Fire Hospital shall be appointed by the Commissioner of the National Fire Agency.

Article 6 (Transitional measure concerning preparation of business plans)
The Establishment Committee may prepare the business plan and budget for the first business year commencing after the establishment of the Fire Hospital.

[Enforcement date: 2021.1.12] Article 6

ADDENDA <Act No. 20863, 2025.4.1>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force three months after the date of its promulgation.

Article 2 (Transitional measure concerning ex officio directors)
Among the directors appointed under the former Article 6 (2) at the time this Act enters into force, the Deputy Commissioner of the National Fire Agency, public officials belonging to the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Ministry of Health and Welfare, and the Administrative Vice Governor of Chungcheongbuk-do shall be deemed ex officio directors under the amended provisions of Article 6 (3).

Article 3 (Transitional measure concerning terms of office of directors other than ex officio directors)
Among the directors appointed under the former Article 6 (2) at the time this Act enters into force, directors who are not ex officio directors under the amended provisions of Article 6 (3) shall be deemed appointed under those amended provisions. In such cases, their term of office shall be the remainder of their previous term.

ADDENDA (GOVERNMENT ORGANIZATION ACT) <Act No. 21065, 2025.10.1>

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation: Provided, That among the Acts amended pursuant to Article 7 of these Addenda, any amendment to an Act promulgated before the enforcement of this Act but not yet in force shall enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant Act; and the following amended provisions shall enter into force on the date specified in each respective subparagraph:
1. The following amended provisions shall enter into force on January 2, 2026: Provided, That among the Acts amended under Article 7 of these Addenda (limited to parts relating to the amended provisions under items (a) and (b)), amendments to Acts promulgated before the enforcement date under the main sentence but not yet in force shall each enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant Act:
(a) The amended provisions of Article 19 (4), Article 23, Article 29 (1) 1, and Article 30;
(b) The amended provisions of Article 12 (2), Article 19 (3), Article 22, and the proviso to Article 29 (2) (limited to parts concerning the Minister of Finance and Economy and the Ministry of Finance and Economy);
(c) The Acts amended under Article 7 of these Addenda (limited to the parts relating to the amended provisions under items (a) and (b)).
2. Omitted.

Articles 2 through 6 Omitted.

Article 7 (Amendments to other Acts)
① through <558> Omitted.
<559> Part of the Act on the Establishment and Operation of the National Fire Hospital shall be amended as follows:
In Article 6 (3) 2, "the Ministry of Economy and Finance and the Ministry of Health and Welfare" shall be replaced with "the Ministry of Health and Welfare and the Ministry of Planning and Budget."
<560> through <626> Omitted.

Article 8 Omitted.

ADDENDA <Act No. 21391, 2026.2.27>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.
